subject: Delegated admin, session controls & SCIM clarifications — Starmap Systems RFI
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@starmapsys.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: security@starmapsys.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Delegated admin & session policy questions (Starmap RFI)

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the RFI response — a few follow-ups from our security and platform teams: we need clarification on two items before we move to procurement.

1) Delegated admin: can Redwood define custom admin roles scoped to org units and limit those roles so they cannot escalate privileges? We need to show separation of duties (e.g., Support Admin vs. Provisioning Admin).

2) Session controls for SSO users: our SAML users are subject to stronger session requirements (session idle timeout, max session duration, re-auth every 12 hours). Can those policies be enforced for both SAML and OIDC federated users?

3) Privileged session recording: do you support live session recording/keystroke logging for console-level admin sessions, and can recordings be exported to customer-managed S3 with retention controls?

4) SCIM: does Redwood support group-scoped SCIM mappings and delta sync for large directories (we plan to provision 40k users)? Also confirm bulk deprovisioning behavior if a user is removed from the source directory.

We're on a tight timeline — can you confirm and share any sample configs or exportable artifacts we can attach to the RFP response?

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Director, Security Architecture
Starmap Systems

Attachments: none
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@starmapsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 12:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Delegated admin & session policy questions (Starmap RFI)

Hi Lena — really appreciate the detailed list. High level answers below and we attached a capability matrix that maps each requirement to our product feature and evidence. Full technical artifacts are linked in the follow-up from Aditya.

Summary:
- Delegated admin: yes. Redwood supports custom admin roles with fine-grained scopes (org/project/model). Role definitions can be marked non-escalating; role assignment is audited and reversible.
- Session controls: session policies (idle timeout, max duration, forced re-auth) can be applied to federated SAML and OIDC sessions and to local accounts. Policies are configured per-authentication realm and can be set at org or workspace scope.
- Privileged session recording: we support admin session recording for console and SSH-like shells in our Dedicated/Private deployments. Recordings can be streamed to customer-managed S3 or retained on the Redwood audit store; retention TTLs and export schedules are configurable.
- SCIM: supports group-scoped mappings, incremental (delta) sync, and bulk operations. Deprovisioning behavior supports immediate account disable plus optional soft-delete window.

I've attached: starmap_rfi_iam_capabilities_matrix.xlsx (matrix + evidence links) and session_recording_playbook.pdf (design and controls). Aditya will follow with SCIM manifest samples and sequence diagrams.

Next steps: can we schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough tomorrow to walk your SRE/security folks through the session recording flow and SCIM bulk sync behaviour?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Lena — quick technical follow-up (pasting key snippets here and attaching a sample SCIM manifest).

On SCIM and provisioning:
- Schema: we support RFC 7643/7644 plus common enterprise extensions (entitlements, manager, employeeNumber). Our group-scoped mappings allow mapping to multiple roles; for example: scim.group.displayName=="prod-admins" -> role:ProvisioningAdmin (scope: project:payment-service).
- Delta sync: incremental sync uses SCIM change events with startIndex/totalResults pagination and supports per-sync concurrency tuning for large directories. We also provide a bulk endpoint for on-demand batch operations (used during initial migrations).
- Deprovision semantics: default is immediate disable (auth blocked) and a configurable soft-delete window (30/90/180 days) where user metadata is retained for audit. During soft-delete we retain KV cache and tokens are revoked.
- Session enforcement: session policy evaluation happens at the token issuance layer for SAML/OIDC (IdP-initiated and SP-initiated). For long-lived refresh tokens we support maximum refresh lifetime enforcement.

Exporting recordings to S3: we stream multipart objects to customer S3 with server-side encryption options; we emit manifest JSON per recording with a signed URL for temporary playback. Retention policies are policy-driven and can be set per-bucket and per-tenant.

Sample artifacts: sample_scim_manifest.json (attached), short design diagram in Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3Cstarmap-iam-matrix

Let me know any specific attributes you want included in the sample mapping and I can produce a 1-page configuration example for tomorrow's walkthrough.

—Aditya
Technical Product Manager, Identity & Access
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sample_scim_manifest.json (application/json)

Sean/Aditya — thanks for the fast turnaround, that helps. Two follow-ups before we lock down the RFP response:

- For session recordings: can you confirm maximum recording retention limit in Dedicated vs Hosted? Also need to show whether recordings can be encrypted with our KMS and whether we can apply a legal hold to specific recordings.

- For SCIM: in the bulk deprovision flow, are external identities removed immediately or disabled and retained for audit? We need to demonstrate that user lockouts will not break historical audit trails.

If you can provide a 1-page config snippet and a short statement we can include in the RFP that describes the default behavior and configurable knobs, that would be ideal.

Cheers,
Lena

Lena — quick commercial note:

1) Retention limits: Hosted (standard) recording retention is 90 days by default (configurable up to 365 days with retention add-on). Dedicated and Private deployments support customer-configurable retention up to 7 years depending on contract and storage tier. All recording exports support SSE-KMS with customer KMS keys in Dedicated/Private.

2) Legal hold & audit: we support legal hold flags that override TTL and prevent deletion. Holds are logged and visible in the audit timeline.

3) SCIM deprovision: default behavior is immediate disable; audit traces and soft-delete metadata are retained for the configured retention window (30/90/180 days). During soft-delete user history and tokens remain available for forensic queries.

Attached: 1-page config snippet (included in the Drive link) and a proposed mutual action plan for the technical walkthrough and evidence handoff. If that looks good we'll send the standard NDA/DocuSign for the deeper artifacts.

Proposed times for the walkthrough: Mon 11 May 14:00 PDT or Tue 12 May 10:00 PDT — which works for your team?

Regards,
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference
